t: Smallest Number With Given Digit Product — Factor Greedily by Large Digits
o: Digits multiply to n. To minimize the number, minimize digit COUNT first, then lexicographic order. Greedily extract the largest digits 9,8,…,2 that divide n; whatever remains must be 1 (or n has prime factor > 7 ⇒ impossible, e.g., 44 = 4·11). Then output the collected digits sorted ascending. n=105 → 9? no; 5, then 7, then 3 → digits {3,5,7} → "357".
k: Greedy division by 9..2 minimizes digit count; sort ascending for the smallest number.

a.i: Repeatedly divide out each digit d from 9 down to 2 while divisible. If the remainder exceeds 1, no answer. Concatenate digits ascending.
s: For d = 9..2, while n % d == 0 record d and divide.
Sort recorded digits ascending and join.
a.t: O(log n · 8) — at most ~60 divisions total
a.sp: O(log n) for the digit list

w: Why greedy is correct: any factorization into digits 2–9 can be refined so that no digit is composite-of-others unnecessarily; extracting large divisors first never increases digit count, and among equal-count candidates ascending order is minimal. Watch big-integer types (n up to 10^18 needs long long / BigInt). Edge cases: n=1, primes 2–7, and primes ≥ 11 → "-1".
